first_impression.reaction: Googled 'seminyak wedding venues' while comparing planners. No 'best' in the title this time, and the intro says 'The order follows the type of venue, not a ranking.' Good start. The table admits gaps with 'Not published' and even flags where a venue's own figures don't agree. Jumped to the FAQ and the money questions. Same hole as every other venue list: not one price, and nothing on how Wedded Wonderland gets paid.

journey.quote: The order follows the type of venue, not a ranking.
journey.reaction: Fine. No fake 'top 7'. I can compare them myself.

journey.section: Which Seminyak wedding venues are worth a look?
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail, and "Ask in writing" means its own figures do not agree.
journey.reaction: They're telling me where the venue's own numbers contradict themselves. That's the kind of thing I'd normally find out the hard way.

journey.quote: None of the seven publishes exclusive use of the whole property, so ask in writing whether your ceremony and reception spaces can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: That's the catch up front, not buried. Exactly what I'd want to know before paying a deposit.

journey.quote: It is the largest wedding operation on this list, with a space for almost every part of a long weekend.
journey.reaction: Largest by what? You've got their space capacities, not how many weddings they run. Say 'largest published spaces' and I'd believe it.
'Deliberately' according to who? You're guessing at the hotel's intent. Just give me the numbers.

journey.quote: Indoor venues, open-air terraces and event lawns take up to 250 guests, a figure given for gatherings in general rather than weddings.
journey.reaction: Good. Qualifies the figure instead of letting me assume 250 at a seated wedding dinner.

journey.quote: The resort's wedding packages are offered for non-legal arrangements only.
journey.reaction: Real catch, plainly stated. Most pages would leave that for the contract.

journey.section: Money and contracts: questions to ask each venue
journey.quote: Is there a minimum spend or venue hire fee, and are service charge and tax included?
journey.reaction: Right question, and the list overall is sharp. But you're handing me homework. Not a single venue price or minimum spend anywhere on the page.

journey.section: Money and contracts: questions to ask each venue
journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to exclusive use, needs an answer in writing before you commit, and your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you sign, through Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: In writing is right; I got burned on exactly that. But this is the spot to tell me what your fee is and whether venues pay you. Silence.

journey.quote: It opens to the public from 10am to 9pm daily, so ask early about private hire and how late music can run.
journey.reaction: Practical, honest trade-off. A public pool club isn't a private venue and they say so.

journey.quote: Standout: A triple-tier dive tower into the pool, which your guests will find before you do.
journey.reaction: Cute line, zero use to me. Capacity and ceremony are both 'Not published' and this is the standout?

journey.section: Resort, villa or pool club: which setting suits you?
journey.quote: For real weddings and settings to compare, browse the free Wedded Wonderland magazines.
journey.reaction: Real weddings, good, but will any of them show the actual budget? A magazine is usually mood boards.

journey.section: When should you marry in Seminyak?
journey.quote: Smartraveller's overall advice for Indonesia is to exercise a high degree of caution, and Bali falls under that overall level.
journey.reaction: A wedding business quoting the government warning level, plus methanol, rips and rabies. Not selling me a fantasy. Trust up.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally get married in Bali?
journey.quote: Persons of any nationality may generally marry in Indonesia if they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government, listed as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian, and both parties must hold the same religion.
journey.reaction: The real legal catch, sourced and dated. Matters for us.

journey.section: Shortlist your Seminyak venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing is good. But payments going through you means money passes your hands. Do you take a cut from the venue? Not answered.

unanswered_questions: What does any of these seven cost? Even one published 'from' package price or minimum spend, with an 'as at' date.
Which venues charge a venue hire fee or minimum spend, and are service charge and tax on top?
Room counts for the resorts, so I know whether 100 guests can actually stay on site.
If both W Bali's Great Room capacity and other figures disagree, what are the real numbers?
Can a couple of different religions, or no religion, legally marry in Bali, or is a symbolic ceremony plus an Australian legal marriage the only route?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'from AUD' for a Seminyak wedding? (deferred business detail)
Do you take commissions or mark-ups from these venues, and will you disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real Seminyak wedding you've planned, with the actual budget. (deferred business detail)
Have you worked with any of these seven directly, or is this compiled from their websites? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: It is the largest wedding operation on this list, with a space for almost every part of a long weekend.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported superlative: the page only has space capacities, not anything about the size of their wedding operation.
Asserts the venue's intent without a source. Opinion dressed as fact.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask each venue for a written quote, then ask:
turn_offs_found.why: Good questions, but the whole page has zero prices. Unquantified costs are where the catch usually hides.

turn_offs_found.quote: Standout: A triple-tier dive tower into the pool, which your guests will find before you do.
turn_offs_found.why: Charm instead of facts, on a venue where capacity and ceremony details are both unpublished.

turn_offs_found.quote: For real weddings and settings to compare, browse the free Wedded Wonderland magazines.
turn_offs_found.why: Promises real weddings but gives no sign of budgets or numbers, which is the proof I actually want.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the guest-count grid and the same-religion rule for a legal marriage in Indonesia
Our Reddit thread: the money and contract questions list, the exclusive-use warning and the Smartraveller points (methanol, wet season, volcanic buffer day)

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Seminyak venues through Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned trust: sourced numbers, gaps admitted, non-legal packages and public opening hours called out, government warnings up front. But no prices, and nothing on how you're paid or whether venues pay you. I'd email those two questions before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Add published cost signals where sources allow: any venue 'from' package price, hire fee or minimum spend with an 'as at' date; where none exists, add a 'Pricing' column saying 'Not published' so the gap is explicit.

Tighten unsupported lines: change W Bali's 'largest wedding operation' to 'largest published spaces', cut 'deliberately' from The Oberoi, and swap the Mrs Sippy dive-tower standout for a useful fact or 'ask' prompt.

Near the Concierge CTAs, state plainly how the fee works and whether supplier commissions apply (deferred business detail), and point the magazine link at a real wedding with its budget if one exists.

Business details (fees, commissions, real weddings, venue relationships) are deferred; voiced as unanswered questions only.
